newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Bunds to withstand rush to strong fx.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Bunds to withstand rush to strong fx.

text.p: International money is moving towards bond markets blessed by strong currencies, yet Bunds remain protected from the impact of a weak mark, analysts said on Monday.

"Bund investors are mainly domestic investors or core European investors for whom Germany is cheaper than other core markets," said Clive Parry, fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley International in London.
"Global investors who are looking for strong currencies have already deserted Bunds for sterling, dollars or lira."
The dollar surged to its strongest level against the mark in almost six years on Monday, while sterling leapt to its highest levels versus the mark since October 1990.

Dealers attributed the mark's weakness to expectations of a broad EMU (European economic and monetary union), following last week's German government approval of a 1997 supplementary budget which allowed the deficit to rise sharply.
Lira also benefited from the strong dollar, testing 970 against the mark.
Italian BTP futures on LIFFE set another record high at the open, at 137.10. The September contract was at 136.48 at 1027 GMT, down 30 basis points on the day.
September Bund futures fell 36 basis points to 102.63, with the markets uneasy at the weaker currency.
"The weak mark has been the catalyst for a correction," said Matt Knowles, German bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in London.
"The market tried and failed last week to break through the 5.5 percent cash yield."
But the market's longer-term prospects are solid, analysts said.
"Bunds continue to benefit from liquidity in France, Italy and Spain -- Italian investors are some of the biggest buyers of Bunds," said Kirit Shah, chief strategist at Sanwa International in London.
Bunds may also benefit from the interest rate picture in Germany, Shah added.
"The BTP/Bund spread could widen to 125 basis points, because the Bundesbank will be forced to raise the repo rate. Convergence will happen, but there are some pitfalls along the way."
The 10-year BTP/Bund spread fell to a record low of 86 basis points on Monday. But German bonds may wobble if the mark weakens beyond its current 1.79 level against the dollar, analysts added.
"If the weak mark continues, the inflationary impact for Germany will affect Bunds," said Parry.
"A move to 1.80-1.90 against the dollar may be worrying."
Gilts, meanwhile, were benefiting from a powerful domestic currency, analysts said.
The September gilt future was 9/32 lower at 114-18, after gaining on Friday on news the Bank of England would not auction any new 10-year gilts in the third quarter.
UK fund managers swung to their most positive stance on gilts for two-and-a-half years, in the wake of the budget on July 2, a survey showed on Monday.
"Sterling's strength has brought strong total returns for bond investors," said Shah.
"Gilts are at the top of the league on a currency-adjusted basis."
Shah said Swedish bonds were among other debt markets to benefit from a stronger currency, with Swedish debt and currency gains moving hand in hand in the past few months.
